prs.notes: Numbered PR 4 in CAMPAIGN.md. Started 26-11-2026, cut from c09a6044156. Implemented the same day: IAsyncMediaRepository (IAsyncContentRepository<IMedia> plus GetMediaByPathAsync, GetByLevelAsync, GetAncestorsAsync, RecycleBinSmellsAsync), AsyncMediaRepository as the first direct subclass of the wide base (media version join, ContentRow projection, StartMediaId nulling as the only kind-specific delete clause, no-op version delete, MediaRefreshNotification, path lookup with the resize suffix stripped by a regex anchored to the final extension), ContentBaseFactory.BuildEntity(NodeDto, ContentVersionDto, IMediaType) and BuildEFCoreMediaVersionDto sharing ResolveMediaPath with the NPoco builder, DI line. Fixture AsyncMediaRepositoryTest: 34 tests (the NPoco fixture's 29 re-expressed against keys and the purpose-built shapes, minus the two filter tests and the tiebreak test, see §8 26-11-2026; plus the media-specific and plain-persist-flow tests of the spec), green on SQLite and SQL Server (banner-verified). Red proof by sabotaging four seams (parent key, start-node clearing, resize suffix, stored path): exactly the tests naming those rules failed. Independent review: no must-fix; applied a regex-only suffix strip (an underscore or dot elsewhere in the path is kept), a NodeId order on the path lookup, a document in the count test, a property edit in the bulk-move test and a property-row count on the EF Core-saved item. Plan corrected: §4b change 7 withdrawn (PR 3's 3be2575a95f keeps the unchanged-save write for media). Committed as 5699e4af13e and opened as draft PR #24808 on 26-11-2026. Second independent review of the PR: no must-fix; applied as 7e12523cde9 (children and descendants paging tests over the media row shape, creator/writer round-trip for unknown and known users, delete test row counts derived from the fixture) and two divergence notes in the PR description (always-joined media version table; stricter rendition suffix strip). Third review (second independent pass, 26-11-2026): no must-fix; its should-fix was a path-lookup case that passed for the wrong reason (the folder-name input was a miss under NPoco's strip too); applied as 02d58d2f441 with a distinguishing input (red-proven by loosening the regex), the shared property-equality helper on the save round-trip, and a real-cache recycle bin test pinning CacheKeys.MediaRecycleBinCacheKey. Third pass: no must-fix; two should-fixes applied as 7327fc8ff06 (blank-name rejection pinned and listed as a divergence; parent-key test compares a two-item read with a single read), tautological cache assertion dropped, filter-parameter contract gap noted in the description for PR 5. Fourth pass: no must-fix; one should-fix (the blank-name rationale was wrong: NPoco auto-names a blank item " (1)" rather than failing to read it back) applied as 653738cf584 with the CS1998 nit, the double-extension clause and the tiebreak note in the description. Fifth pass found a must-fix: PerformDeleteVersionAsync was a bare no-op, so deleting a media item's current version by id succeeded silently where NPoco's ContentRepositoryBase.DeleteVersion and the publishable EF Core hook throw. Fixed as 83630724b17 (the hook reads the version's Current flag and refuses a current one; red-proven against the old hook) with a test and a description line. Fixture 40 tests, green on SQLite and SQL Server. Sixth pass (26-11-2026): no must-fix, no should-fix, every description claim verified; review loop closed at 83630724b17. Remaining nits deliberately left: relative command count in the parent-key test, double-extension path case not asserted, null-name row reads as empty string, NodeId order on the path lookup unlisted, dead count argument on the regex Replace, parameter order of BuildEFCoreMediaVersionDto. The sort-order tiebreak test was not mirrored: the tiebreak lives in the base's ordering helper, which has its own unit test.
